findings.note: A player could pair Spider with Fang (a spider's own venomous organ) as a creature/body-part match, competing with the intended Spider:Exoskeleton pairing and leaving Fang stranded from Spinneret.

notes:
Spider's fang is a plausible creature-part answer that competes with Spider:Exoskeleton, stranding Fang from Spinneret in the instrument-action set. Swap one word to remove the overlap.
- set-creature-part: Spider:Exoskeleton competes with Spider:Fang (fang is also a spider body part), stranding Fang from Spinneret in the other set.
  Try: Replace Spider with a different creature whose defining part is unambiguous and not shared with the instrument-action set, e.g. Beetle:Exoskeleton (beetle already appears elsewhere as a conversion endpoint, so prefer a creature not used in set-conversion — consider Ant:Exoskeleton if Ant is unused) paired with Moth:Antenna
  Or: Keep Spider but change the paired part from Exoskeleton to a part that is not also tied to venom/fangs, e.g. Spider:Spinneret — but this then collides with set-instrument-action's Spinneret:Spin, so this option requires also changing set-instrument-action's organ (not permitted here)
  Or: Replace Exoskeleton with Antenna-equivalent unique-to-spider feature e.g. Spider:Pedipalp, keeping Moth:Antenna, so Spider is still paired with a part distinct from Fang
- set-instrument-action: Fang (paired with Spinneret) is also a plausible creature-part answer for Spider, creating a cross-set collision that strands Fang.
  Try: Replace Fang with a different organ-action pair within spider anatomy that doesn't double as a creature-part answer, e.g. Spinneret:Spin paired with Chelicera:Inject (chelicerae are the actual injecting organ, less likely to be picked as 'the' defining spider part over exoskeleton)
  Or: Replace Fang with Spinneret's counterpart from a different creature already in the board's insect world, e.g. Proboscis:Siphon (moth's feeding organ) paired with Spinneret:Spin, keeping the organ-action grain intact
  Or: Keep Fang but change its action pairing is not enough — the fix must replace Fang itself since the word choice is the collision source
Do not change: set-conversion, set-before-after — no allowlisted finding touches them.

persisted.note: Reading the right pair in reverse order (Weave:Sunset) gives the same start-of-span:end-of-span relation as the left pair (Sunrise:Tear), so a player could defend Sunrise:Tear::Weave:Sunset as a valid 'start and end of a span' analogy even though it mixes the day-cycle and fabric-cycle instances. Both halves read as: "Sunrise (start of a span) to Tear (end of a span) — a start:end relation" and "Sunset (end) to Weave (start) as written is end:start, but read in reverse as Weave:Sunset it becomes start:end".
